guide.q.owner_vs_manager: What's the difference between an owner and a manager?
guide.a.owner_vs_manager: Owners have full access: listings, calendar, groups, questions, holidays, users, site pages, settings, API keys, sessions, and the activity log. Managers can manage listings, view the calendar, manage groups, issue refunds, and view the activity log. They cannot change settings, manage users, manage questions or holidays, create API keys, edit site pages, or view sessions.
guide.a.editor_role:
Editors are content-only collaborators. They can create and edit listings and groups. They can also edit public site pages when Site is enabled.

Editors cannot view attendees, income, costs, or Money. They cannot change settings, manage users, or use the API. An editor has no key for reading attendee details. This protects personal data even if someone bypasses the hidden pages.
guide.q.agent_role: What can a Delivery agent do?
guide.a.agent_role: Delivery agents are a restricted login that only ever sees their own delivery run sheet (/admin/deliveries) — the drop-offs and collections for the logistics agents they are assigned to. They cannot reach any other admin page.
guide.q.invite_admin: How do I invite another admin?
guide.a.invite_admin: Go to Users, enter a username and choose their role (owner, manager, editor, or delivery agent). You'll receive an invite link to send them. They use the link to set their password and activate their account.
guide.q.invite_link_expiry: How long do invite links last?
guide.a.invite_link_expiry: Invite links expire after 7 days. If the link expires before the person uses it, you'll need to delete the pending user and create a new invite.
guide.a.attendee_data_protection: All personal information (names, email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses) is encrypted before being stored. Even if the database were compromised, the data cannot be read without the encryption keys. Data is only decrypted when an authenticated admin views it.
guide.a.encryption_overview:
Different kinds of data get different protection, so the system stays both secure and usable:

  • Attendee contact details are doubly secured by your password. Names, email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses and the free-text answers people type into booking questions are protected with two keys at once — the server's encryption key as well as a key derived from your account password. A stolen copy of the database, even together with the server's key, can't reveal them; only an admin signed in with their password can decrypt them. Pre-set multiple-choice answers are saved as a reference and protected by the server's key, like the listing details below.
  • Listing details are encrypted at rest in the database. Listing names, descriptions, locations, dates, images and links are encrypted with the server's encryption key before they are written, so the stored database never holds them in readable form.
  • Operational numbers are deliberately left unencrypted. Figures such as income and availability/capacity are stored as plain values because the database itself has to total them, compare them and check remaining places. They hold no personal information, so keeping them readable lets reports and capacity checks run without unlocking anything.
guide.q.privacy_first_by_default: Why is this privacy-first instead of a CRM?
guide.a.privacy_first_by_default:
The system deliberately stops short of being a CRM. It keeps the booking data you need, encrypts attendee details, and uses irreversible contact hashes for unsubscribe, contact history, and returning-customer rules. That helps with GDPR and UK GDPR obligations around data minimisation, purpose limitation, retention, and erasure.

That design protects attendees and the owner: it does not remove your legal obligations, but it reduces the personal data and profiling you are responsible for. If you want a fuller CRM, listing webhooks are a good place to start - send booking events to a separate system designed for that job.
guide.q.lost_password: What happens if I lose my password?
guide.a.lost_password: There is no password recovery. If you lose your password, you cannot log in or decrypt any data. Keep your password safe. Another owner can delete your account and send a fresh invite, and all existing attendee data remains accessible to other admins.
guide.a.export_attendee_data: Yes. On any listing's attendee list, click Export CSV. The export includes name, email, phone, address, special instructions, quantity, registration date, amount paid, transaction ID, check-in status, ticket token, and ticket URL. If the listing has custom booking questions, each question is appended as an additional column (one per question, in the order assigned to the listing) with the attendee's selected answer text. For daily listings, the attendee list has a date filter — select a date to see only that day's attendees, and the CSV export respects the same filter.
guide.a.reset_database: It permanently deletes everything: all listings, attendees, groups, questions, users, holidays, API keys, activity logs, payment configuration, and sessions. The system returns to its initial setup state. You must type a confirmation phrase to proceed. This cannot be undone.
guide.a.what_are_webhooks: Webhooks send an automatic notification to a URL of your choice whenever someone registers for a listing. You can use them to connect to other services, e.g. sending a Slack message or updating a spreadsheet.
guide.q.setup_webhook: How do I set up a webhook?
guide.a.setup_webhook:
Add a webhook URL when creating or editing a listing. Every time someone books that listing, a POST request is sent to your URL with the attendee's details.

If one booking would send to more than 16 different URLs, the system sends none of its webhooks. It records a delivery failure in the activity log.

guide.a.what_are_sessions: A session is created each time an admin logs in. Sessions expire after 24 hours. You can view all active sessions from the Sessions page.
guide.q.logout_other_users: How do I log out other users?
guide.a.logout_other_users: On the Sessions page, click "Log out of all other sessions". This ends every session except your own, forcing all other admins to log in again. Useful if you suspect an account has been compromised.
guide.a.what_is_calendar: The Calendar page lets you pick a date and see every attendee booked across all listings on that day. This is especially useful for daily listings. You can export a CSV of the day's attendees and manage check-ins, edits, and deletions from the same view.
guide.a.what_is_activity_log: The Log page shows a chronological list of admin actions such as listing creation, listing updates, attendee changes, and question changes. Both owners and managers can view the log. Each listing also has its own log, accessible from the listing page, showing only actions related to that listing.
guide.q.why_am_i_locked_out_even_though: Why am I locked out even though my password is correct?
guide.a.why_am_i_locked_out_even_though: You've likely hit the rate limit from previous failed attempts. The lockout applies to your IP address, not your account, so other admins logging in from different locations are not affected. Wait 15 minutes and try again.
guide.q.is_there_a_way_to_recover_a: Is there a way to recover a lost password?
guide.a.is_there_a_way_to_recover_a: No. There is no password recovery mechanism. All attendee data is encrypted with keys derived from admin passwords, so a reset would make existing data unreadable. If you lose your password, another owner can delete your account and send a fresh invite — all existing attendee data remains accessible to other admins. Keep your password somewhere safe.
guide.a.how_are_admin_sessions_secured: Sessions use HttpOnly cookies that cannot be read by JavaScript. Each session expires after 24 hours, after which you must log in again. You can view all active sessions and log out all other sessions from the Sessions page if you suspect your account has been compromised.
guide.q.how_do_i_log_out_other_users: How do I log out other users?
guide.a.how_do_i_log_out_other_users: On the Sessions page, click "Log out of all other sessions". This ends every session except your own, forcing all other admins to log in again. Useful if you suspect an account has been compromised.
guide.q.what_happens_if_i_enter_the_wron: What happens if I enter the wrong password?
guide.a.what_happens_if_i_enter_the_wron: After 5 failed login attempts from the same IP address, the system locks out that IP for 15 minutes. During the lockout, all login attempts from that IP are rejected — even with the correct password. Wait for the lockout period to pass and try again.
guide.q.what_happens_when_i_change_my_pa: What happens when I change my password?
guide.a.what_happens_when_i_change_my_pa:
Changing your password ends every active session for your account — you and anyone else signed in as you will be logged out and must sign in again with the new password.

Your existing attendee data remains fully accessible. The encryption key is re-secured with the new password, so every record created before the change can still be decrypted after you log back in.
